title: Contractor Estimate Template: Fill In, Download PDF, Word, Excel
description: Write a construction or remodel estimate online with scope, allowances, exclusions and deposit. No sign-up. US project price ranges, with sources.
lede_html: Write a remodel or construction estimate here and download it as a PDF, Word or Excel file. No account is needed. The sample is a kitchen. Enter your own job.

sample.scope: Remodel a 160 sq ft kitchen: demolition, new cabinets and quartz top, under-cabinet lights, tile backsplash, LVP floor, paint.
sample.exclusions: Appliances, moving gas or main drain lines, asbestos or mold work, repairs to hidden structural damage.
sample.terms: Allowances are shown per line. Changes need a signed change order before the work.

items.d: Electrical and plumbing rough-in by licensed subs

must_show.heading: What a contractor estimate should say
must_show.intro_html: A remodel estimate has to be specific enough that two contractors could price the same work. It names the scope, allowances, exclusions, schedule and payment steps.
must_show.why_label: Why it matters on a remodel
rows: The customer sees what the number buys.
Say the amount and who pays when the choice costs more.
List what a homeowner might assume, such as appliances or hidden damage.
A start date and a duration.
Tie payments to stages. Check any deposit limit in your state.
The FTC tells customers to choose licensed and insured contractors, so print the number.

example.heading: Filled example: 12 x 14 room addition
example.intro_html: A different job with sample amounts. Price your own numbers.
example.after_html: The total sits inside the $37,549–$97,843 range from Homeyou.

line_items.heading: Contractor projects and typical prices
line_items.intro_html: Tap Add to put a line on the form. The range comes from the source in the same row. The price that the button adds is a sample inside that range, not a price recommendation.
line_items.after_html: Cost to Build a House puts a general contractor fee at 10–20% of the total project.

rules.heading: Rules to check before you send a contractor estimate

items.title: A signed estimate may become the contract
items.html: New Jersey requires a written contract for home improvement sales over $500, and all changes must also be in writing. Check whether your signed estimate meets the contract rules of your state.

items.title: Cancel period at the home
items.html: A buyer may cancel a sale made at the home until midnight of the third business day after the sale, under the FTC rule. It has limits, so read it if you sign at the kitchen table.

items.title: Deposit limit in California
items.html: The down payment on a home improvement job there is capped at the lesser of $1,000 or 10 percent, except for blanket-bond licensees. The sample deposit is only an example.

faq.q: What is a good contingency line?
faq.a: It depends on your scope and the age of the home. Show it on its own line and say how you will use it. Bring unused amounts back to the customer.
Choose what your contract needs. If you bill cost plus a fee, put the fee on its own line. On a fixed price, give one number per stage.
Enter a line with the unit set to allowance. In the terms, say that the customer pays the difference when the choice costs more, and gets a credit when it costs less.

faq.q: Do I need a separate contract as well?
faq.a: It depends on your state. New Jersey, for example, requires a written contract for home improvement sales over $500. This form does not add contract terms. Ask a local lawyer.
